title: Week 38 Listening: Evaluating Policy Claims at a Community Transport Forum
instructions: 本材料为模拟教学练习，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何官方分数。请先听录音（或阅读文字稿），完成10道听力题；然后学习语法讲解并完成8道语法题；最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。听力题中，单选题请选出最佳答案；填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Maya: Welcome to the Riverside Community Transport Forum. I'm Maya Chen, and today we're evaluating three policy claims about our local bus network. First, let me introduce our speakers: Daniel Ortiz from the city planning office, and Priya Nair, who chairs the residents' committee. Daniel, can you start with the first claim?

Daniel: Thanks, Maya. Claim one says the new bus lane on Mill Street reduced average journey times by fifteen minutes. That's not accurate. Our data shows the reduction was about five minutes during peak hours, not fifteen. The fifteen-minute figure came from a single test run on a Sunday morning with almost no traffic. So the claim overstates the benefit.

Priya: I'd like to add something there. Residents have told us the bus lane helps, but the improvement is modest. Several people said their morning commute is now about eight minutes shorter, which is good, but not fifteen. Also, the bus lane is only on the northbound side, so southbound buses still get stuck near the market.

Maya: Good point. Let's move to claim two. It says the new ticket machines at Central Station accept cash. Is that correct?

Daniel: Partly. The machines accept coins, but not paper notes. So if you only have a ten-pound note, you can't use the machine. You have to go to the ticket counter, which closes at six in the evening. After six, passengers with only notes cannot buy a ticket at the station.

Priya: And that's a real problem for older residents. Many of them prefer cash. The committee has asked the council to add note acceptance, but there's no date for that yet.

Maya: Thank you. Now claim three: the weekend bus service to the hospital runs every twenty minutes. Daniel?

Daniel: That claim is false. On Saturdays, the bus runs every thirty minutes. On Sundays, it runs every forty minutes. The twenty-minute frequency applies only on weekdays. So the weekend service is less frequent than the claim suggests.

Priya: I checked the timetable myself last Saturday. I waited thirty-five minutes because one bus was cancelled. So even the thirty-minute schedule isn't always reliable.

Maya: Let's compare the three claims. Which one is most misleading, in your view?

Daniel: I'd say claim one, because it uses a number from an unusual test run and presents it as typical. Claim two is partly true, and claim three is simply wrong about the frequency.

Priya: I agree that claim one is the most misleading. But I'd add that claim two has the biggest daily impact on vulnerable passengers. So the claims differ in both accuracy and impact.

Maya: That's a useful distinction. Before we finish, can you summarize the changes since last year?

Daniel: Yes. Since last year, the number of bus lanes has increased from two to three. Average journey times have fallen slightly, by about three minutes overall. And the number of ticket machines has grown from four to seven, though most still don't accept notes.

Priya: Also, the residents' committee has grown from twelve members to twenty. We now meet once a month instead of every two months. So public involvement is increasing.

Maya: Thank you both. To conclude: claim one overstates a benefit, claim two is only partly correct, and claim three is false for weekends. We'll publish these findings on the forum website next week.

questions.prompt: What does Daniel say about the fifteen-minute figure in claim one?
options: It came from a single test run on a Sunday morning.
It came from the residents' committee survey.
It came from the weekend hospital bus timetable.
It came from the ticket counter records.
answers: It came from a single test run on a Sunday morning.
questions.explanation: Daniel 明确说十五分钟这个数字来自周日早上的单次测试运行。
questions.evidence: The fifteen-minute figure came from a single test run on a Sunday morning with almost no traffic.

questions.prompt: According to Daniel, what was the actual reduction in journey time during peak hours?
questions.explanation: Daniel 说高峰时段实际减少约五分钟。
questions.evidence: Our data shows the reduction was about five minutes during peak hours, not fifteen.

questions.prompt: What limitation of the new ticket machines does Daniel mention?
options: They accept coins but not paper notes.
They accept notes but not coins.
They are only at the hospital.
answers: They accept coins but not paper notes.
questions.explanation: Daniel 说机器接受硬币但不接受纸币。
questions.evidence: The machines accept coins, but not paper notes.

questions.prompt: What is the frequency of the bus to the hospital on Saturdays?
questions.explanation: Daniel 说周六每三十分钟一班。
questions.evidence: On Saturdays, the bus runs every thirty minutes.

questions.prompt: Which claim do both Daniel and Priya agree is the most misleading?
questions.explanation: Daniel 和 Priya 都认为第一条声明最误导。
questions.evidence: Priya: I agree that claim one is the most misleading.

questions.prompt: What does Priya say about the impact of claim two?
options: It has the biggest daily impact on vulnerable passengers.
It has no impact on anyone.
It is the most misleading claim.
answers: It has the biggest daily impact on vulnerable passengers.
questions.explanation: Priya 说第二条声明对弱势乘客的日常影响最大。
questions.evidence: But I'd add that claim two has the biggest daily impact on vulnerable passengers.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the transcript: Since last year, the number of bus lanes has increased from two to ______.
questions.explanation: Daniel 说公交车道从两条增加到三条。
questions.evidence: Since last year, the number of bus lanes has increased from two to three.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the transcript: The residents' committee has grown from twelve members to ______.
questions.explanation: Priya 说居民委员会成员从十二人增加到二十人。
questions.evidence: Also, the residents' committee has grown from twelve members to twenty.

questions.prompt: What does Priya say about the committee's meeting frequency now?
options: They meet once a month instead of every two months.
They meet every two months instead of once a month.
answers: They meet once a month instead of every two months.
questions.explanation: Priya 说现在每月开会一次，而不是每两个月一次。
questions.evidence: We now meet once a month instead of every two months.

questions.prompt: What will happen next week according to Maya?
options: The findings will be published on the forum website.
The ticket machines will accept notes.
The weekend bus will run every twenty minutes.
The bus lane will be extended southbound.
answers: The findings will be published on the forum website.
questions.explanation: Maya 说下周将在论坛网站发布这些发现。
questions.evidence: We'll publish these findings on the forum website next week.

grammar.title: 位置介词、顺序表达、比较与变化描述
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 位置介词（on, at, near, from...to...）表示地点和范围；2) 顺序表达（first, then, before, after, finally）组织信息；3) 比较结构（more/less...than, the most...）比较事物；4) 变化描述（increase from...to..., grow from...to..., fall by...）说明数量变化。注意区分：新学形式是“变化描述”中的 from...to... 结构；复习形式是位置介词 on/at/near。
grammar.example: Since last year, the number of bus lanes has increased from two to three.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: The new ticket machine is ______ the station entrance.
questions.explanation: 表示在某个具体地点用 at。
questions.evidence: The new ticket machine is at the station entrance.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: The bus stop is ______ the hospital.
questions.evidence: The bus stop is near the hospital.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sequence word: ______, check the timetable. Then buy your ticket.
Choose the correct comparison: The weekend bus is ______ frequent than the weekday bus.
questions.explanation: 比较级用 less...than 表示不如。
questions.evidence: The weekend bus is less frequent than the weekday bus.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct superlative: Claim one is the ______ misleading of the three claims.
questions.explanation: 最高级用 the most + 形容词。
questions.evidence: Claim one is the most misleading of the three claims.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE WORD: The number of ticket machines has grown ______ four to seven.
questions.explanation: 变化描述用 from...to... 结构。
questions.evidence: The number of ticket machines has grown from four to seven.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE WORD: Average journey times have fallen ______ about three minutes.
questions.explanation: 表示下降的幅度用 by。
questions.evidence: Average journey times have fallen by about three minutes.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sequence word: Buy your ticket ______ you get on the bus.
questions.evidence: Buy your ticket before you get on the bus.
